욥기-41-1.title: 욥기 41장 1절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-1.exegesis: 15-24. God shows that if Job cannot bring under control the lower animals (of which he selects the two most striking, behemoth on land, leviathan in the water), much less is he capable of governing the world. behemoth-- The description in part agrees with the hippopotamus, in part with the elephant, but exactly in all details with neither. It is rather a poetical personification of the great Pachydermata, or Herbivora (so "he eateth grass"), the idea of the hippopotamus being predominant. In Job 40:17 , "the tail like a cedar," hardly applies to the latter (so also Job 40:20 , 23 , "Jordan," a river which elephants alone could reach, but see on Job 40:23 ). On the other hand, Job 40:21 , 22 are characteristic of the amphibious river horse. So leviathan (the twisting animal), Job 41:1 , is a generalized term for cetacea, pythons, saurians of the neighboring seas and rivers, including the crocodile, which is the most prominent, and is often associated with the river horse by old writers. "Behemoth" seems to be the Egyptian Pehemout, "water-ox," Hebraized, so-called as being like an ox, whence the Italian bombarino. with thee-- as I made thyself. Yet how great the difference! The manifold wisdom and power of God! he eateth grass-- marvellous in an animal living so much in the water; also strange, that such a monster should not be carnivorous.

욥기-41-2.title: 욥기 41장 2절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 41 Job 41:1-34 . 1. leviathan-- literally, "the twisted animal," gathering itself in folds: a synonym to the Thannin ( Job 3:8 , Margin; see Psa 74:14 ; type of the Egyptian tyrant; Psa 104:26 ; Is 27:1 ; the Babylon tyrant). A poetical generalization for all cetacean, serpentine, and saurian monsters (see on Job 40:15 , hence all the description applies to no one animal); especially the crocodile; which is naturally described after the river horse, as both are found in the Nile. tongue ... lettest down?-- The crocodile has no tongue, or a very small one cleaving to the lower jaw. But as in fishing the tongue of the fish draws the baited hook to it, God asks, Canst thou in like manner take leviathan?

욥기-41-3.title: 욥기 41장 3절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-3.exegesis: 2. hook-- rather, "a rope of rushes." thorn-- rather, a "ring" or "hook." So wild beasts were led about when caught ( Is 37:29 ; Eze 29:4 ); fishes also were secured thus and thrown into the water to keep them alive.

욥기-41-4.title: 욥기 41장 4절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-4.exegesis: 3. soft words-- that thou mayest spare his life. No: he is untamable.
욥기-41-4.theologicalNote: 3. soft words-- that thou mayest spare his life. No: he is untamable.

욥기-41-5.title: 욥기 41장 5절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-5.exegesis: 4. Can he be tamed for domestic use (so Job 39:10-12 )?
욥기-41-5.theologicalNote: 4. Can he be tamed for domestic use (so Job 39:10-12 )?

욥기-41-7.title: 욥기 41장 7절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-7.exegesis: 6. Rather, "partners" (namely, in fishing). make a banquet-- The parallelism rather supports Umbreit, "Do partners (in trade) desire to purchase him?" So the Hebrew ( De 2:6 ). merchants-- literally, "Canaanites," who were great merchants ( Ho 12:7 , Margin).

욥기-41-8.title: 욥기 41장 8절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-8.exegesis: 7. His hide is not penetrable, as that of fishes.
욥기-41-8.theologicalNote: 7. His hide is not penetrable, as that of fishes.

욥기-41-9.title: 욥기 41장 9절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-9.exegesis: 8. If thou lay ... thou wilt have reason ever to remember ... and thou wilt never try it again.
욥기-41-9.theologicalNote: 8. If thou lay ... thou wilt have reason ever to remember ... and thou wilt never try it again.

욥기-41-10.title: 욥기 41장 10절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-10.exegesis: 9. the hope-- of taking him. cast down-- with fear "at the (mere) sight of him."
욥기-41-10.theologicalNote: 9. the hope-- of taking him. cast down-- with fear "at the (mere) sight of him."

욥기-41-11.title: 욥기 41장 11절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-11.exegesis: 10. fierce-- courageous. If a man dare attack one of My creatures ( Ge 49:9 ; Nu 24:9 ), who will dare (as Job has wished) oppose himself ( Psa 2:2 ) to Me, the Creator? This is the main drift of the description of leviathan.
욥기-41-11.theologicalNote: 10. fierce-- courageous. If a man dare attack one of My creatures ( Ge 49:9 ; Nu 24:9 ), who will dare (as Job has wished) oppose himself ( Psa 2:2 ) to Me, the Creator? This is the main drift of the description of leviathan.

욥기-41-12.title: 욥기 41장 12절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-12.exegesis: 11. prevented-- done Me a favor first: anticipated Me with service ( Psa 21:3 ). None can call Me to account ("stand before Me," Job 41:10 ) as unjust, because I have withdrawn favors from him (as in Job's case): for none has laid Me under a prior obligation by conferring on Me something which was not already My own. What can man give to Him who possesses all, including man himself? Man cannot constrain the creature to be his "servant" ( Job 41:4 ), much less the Creator.

욥기-41-13.title: 욥기 41장 13절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-13.exegesis: 12. I will not conceal-- a resumption of the description broken off by the digression, which formed an agreeable change. his power-- literally, "the way," that is, true proportion or expression of his strength (so Hebrew, De 19:4 ). comely proportion-- literally, "the comeliness of his structure" (his apparatus: so "suit of apparel" Jud 17:10 ) [Maurer]. Umbreit translates, "his armor." But that follows after.

욥기-41-14.title: 욥기 41장 14절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-14.exegesis: 13. discover-- rather, "uncover the surface" of his garment (skin, Job 10:11 ): strip off the hard outer coat with which the inner skin is covered. with-- rather, "within his double jaws"; literally, "bridle"; hence that into which the bridle is put, the double row of teeth; but "bridle" is used to imply that none dare put his hand in to insert a bridle where in other animals it is placed ( Job 41:4 ; 39:10 ).

욥기-41-15.title: 욥기 41장 15절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-15.exegesis: 14. doors of ... face-- his mouth. His teeth are sixty in number, larger in proportion than his body, some standing out, some serrated, fitting into each other like a comb [Bochart].
욥기-41-15.theologicalNote: 14. doors of ... face-- his mouth. His teeth are sixty in number, larger in proportion than his body, some standing out, some serrated, fitting into each other like a comb [Bochart].

욥기-41-16.title: 욥기 41장 16절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-16.exegesis: 15. Rather, his "furrows of shields" (as "tubes," "channels," see on Job 40:18 ), are, &c., that is, the rows of scales, like shields covering him: he has seventeen such rows. shut up-- firmly closed together. A musket ball cannot penetrate him, save in the eye, throat, and belly.

욥기-41-19.title: 욥기 41장 19절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-19.exegesis: 18. Translate: "his sneezing, causeth a light to shine." Amphibious animals, emerging after having long held their breath under water, respire by violently expelling the breath like one sneezing: in the effort the eyes which are usually directed towards the sun, seem to flash fire; or it is the expelled breath that, in the sun, seems to emit light. eyelids of morning-- The Egyptian hieroglyphics paint the eyes of the crocodile as the symbol for morning, because the eyes appear the first thing, before the whole body emerges from the deep [Horæ Hierogliphicæ 1.65. Bochart].

욥기-41-20.title: 욥기 41장 20절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-20.exegesis: 19. burning lamps-- "torches"; namely, in respiring ( Job 41:18 ), seem to go out.
욥기-41-20.theologicalNote: 19. burning lamps-- "torches"; namely, in respiring ( Job 41:18 ), seem to go out.

욥기-41-21.title: 욥기 41장 21절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-21.exegesis: 20. seething-- boiling: literally, "blown under," under which a fire is blown.
욥기-41-21.theologicalNote: 20. seething-- boiling: literally, "blown under," under which a fire is blown.

욥기-41-23.title: 욥기 41장 23절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-23.exegesis: 22. remaineth-- abideth permanently. His chief strength is in the neck. sorrow-- anxiety or dismay personified. is turned into joy-- rather, "danceth," "exulteth"; wherever he goes, he spreads terror "before him."
욥기-41-23.theologicalNote: 22. remaineth-- abideth permanently. His chief strength is in the neck. sorrow-- anxiety or dismay personified. is turned into joy-- rather, "danceth," "exulteth"; wherever he goes, he spreads terror "before him."

욥기-41-24.title: 욥기 41장 24절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-24.exegesis: 23. flakes-- rather, "dewlaps"; that which falls down (Margin). They are "joined" fast and firm, together, not hanging loose, as in the ox. are firm-- Umbreit and Maurer, "are spread." in themselves-- rather, "upon him."

욥기-41-25.title: 욥기 41장 25절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-25.exegesis: 24. heart-- "In large beasts which are less acute in feeling, there is great firmness of the heart, and slower motion" [Bochart]. The nether millstone, on which the upper turns, is especially hard.
욥기-41-25.theologicalNote: 24. heart-- "In large beasts which are less acute in feeling, there is great firmness of the heart, and slower motion" [Bochart]. The nether millstone, on which the upper turns, is especially hard.

욥기-41-26.title: 욥기 41장 26절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-26.exegesis: 25. he-- the crocodile; a type of the awe which the Creator inspires when He rises in wrath. breakings-- namely, of the mind, that is, terror. purify themselves-- rather, "they wander from the way," that is, flee away bewildered [Maurer and Umbreit].

욥기-41-27.title: 욥기 41장 27절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-27.exegesis: 26. cannot hold-- on his hard skin. habergeon-- coat of mail; avail must be taken by zeugma out of "hold," as the verb in the second clause: "hold" cannot apply to the "coat of mail."
욥기-41-27.theologicalNote: 26. cannot hold-- on his hard skin. habergeon-- coat of mail; avail must be taken by zeugma out of "hold," as the verb in the second clause: "hold" cannot apply to the "coat of mail."

욥기-41-29.title: 욥기 41장 29절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-29.exegesis: 28. arrow-- literally, "son of the bow"; Oriental imagery ( La 3:13 ; Margin). stubble-- Arrows produce no more effect than it would to throw stubble at him.
욥기-41-29.theologicalNote: 28. arrow-- literally, "son of the bow"; Oriental imagery ( La 3:13 ; Margin). stubble-- Arrows produce no more effect than it would to throw stubble at him.

욥기-41-30.title: 욥기 41장 30절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-30.exegesis: 29. Darts-- rather, "clubs"; darts have been already mentioned ( Job 41:26 ).
욥기-41-30.theologicalNote: 29. Darts-- rather, "clubs"; darts have been already mentioned ( Job 41:26 ).

욥기-41-31.title: 욥기 41장 31절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-31.exegesis: 30. stones-- rather, "potsherds," that is, the sharp and pointed scales on the belly, like broken pieces of pottery. sharp-pointed things-- rather, "a threshing instrument," but not on the fruits of the earth, but "on the mire"; irony. When he lies on the mire, he leaves the marks of his scales so imprinted on it, that one might fancy a threshing instrument with its sharp teeth had been drawn over it ( Is 28:27 ).

욥기-41-32.title: 욥기 41장 32절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-32.exegesis: 31. Whenever he moves. sea-- the Nile ( Is 19:5 ; Na 3:8 ). pot of ointment-- the vessel in which it is mixed. Appropriate to the crocodile, which emits a musky smell.

욥기-41-33.title: 욥기 41장 33절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-41-33.exegesis: 32. path-- the foam on his track. hoary-- as hair of the aged.
욥기-41-33.theologicalNote: 32. path-- the foam on his track. hoary-- as hair of the aged.
